newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Q1 private wage deals pay 4.8 pct rises.
newsitem.headline: Australia Q1 private wage deals pay 4.8 pct rises.

text.p: Australian private sector enterprise wage deals concluded in the March quarter granted average annualised wage increases of 4.8 percent, up from 4.4 percent in the December quarter, the Industrial Relations Department said on Wednesday.
Overall, enterprise wage deals in all sectors concluded in the March quarter paid average annualised rises of 4.7 percent, up from 4.4 percent in the December quarter.
The department said at least 967 enterprise bargaining agreements, covering an estimated 94,400 employees, were formalised by the Industrial Relations Commission in the March quarter.

All enterprise agreements current at March 31 -- not just the new ones concluded in the quarter -- paid average annualised wage increases (AAWI) of 4.8 percent for all employees, up from 4.6 percent in the previous three months.
All current agreements in just the private sector paid 4.9 percent average annualised rises, up from 4.8 percent previously.

"While the quarterly AAWI series is a useful forward indicator of the average increase paid by new federal agreements, less than three percent of all employees on average are covered by each quarter's figures," the department said in its release.
"By contrast, the all current AAWI estimate covers a much larger group (about 15 percent, but down from 18 percent in the December quarter)," it said.
